options_only.score: 200/200 (100%); K 192/192, S 8/8, G 0/0. The overall rate is inflated: the reviewer had already read every stem in the blind pass, so the 82% ceiling check is not meaningful here. The S hits are judged on the options alone.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '$2,500' appears in 2 options and 'per invoice or item' in 3; the key is the only option with both.
findings.fix: Parallel distractors that do not share the key's parts, e.g. $2,500 per invoice or item / $5,000 per invoice or item / $1,000 per invoice or item / $500 per invoice or item (vary only the amount).

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '80%' in 2 options and 'of vote and of other shares' in 2; the key is their intersection.
findings.fix: Vary one dimension only, e.g. 80% of vote and of other shares / 50% ... / 66 2/3% ... / 90% ..., or keep the and/or contrast but use the same percentage throughout.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: 'More than 50%' in 2 options and 'of each' in 3; the key is the only one with both.
findings.fix: Make distractors parallel: More than 50% of each / At least 80% of each / More than 25% of each / At least 66 2/3% of each.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '25% of wages' in 2 options and '2.5% of UBIA' in 3; the key is the intersection.
findings.fix: Change one element per distractor without a shared majority, e.g. 25% of wages plus 2.5% of UBIA / 20% of wages plus 5% of UBIA / 30% of wages plus 3% of UBIA / 15% of wages plus 10% of UBIA.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '$5 a square foot' in 3 options and 'up to 300 sq ft' in 2; the key is the intersection.
findings.fix: e.g. $5 up to 300 / $4 up to 250 / $6 up to 200 / $3 up to 400 square feet.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '100 or fewer' in 2 options and 'eligible partners' in 2; the key is the intersection.
findings.fix: e.g. 100 or fewer eligible partners / 200 or fewer eligible partners / 50 or fewer eligible partners / 35 or fewer eligible partners.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '50' in 2 options and 'full-time and equivalent employees' in 3; the key is the intersection.
findings.fix: Keep the counting phrase in all four and vary only the number (25, 50, 75, 100), or vary only the counting phrase at 50.

findings.issue: Convergence cue: '14 days' in 3 options and '10% of days rented' in 2; the key is the intersection.
findings.fix: e.g. 14 days or 10% of days rented / 30 days or 15% of days rented / 7 days or 5% of days rented / 21 days or 20% of days rented.

findings.issue: January 31, 2026 is a Saturday, so the actual 2025 W-2 Copy A due date is the next business day, February 2, 2026 (the IRS states the rolled date: the 2026 General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 give February 1, 2027 for 2026 forms). Key is still the best option offered, but the stem asks for the dated deadline.
findings.fix: Ask for the general rule ('Form W-2 Copy A is due to the SSA by:' with options January 31 / February 28 / March 31 / February 15 of the following year), or make the key February 2, 2026 and say why in the explanation.

findings.issue: Minor: March 15, 2026 is a Sunday. The 2 1/2-month rule (Temp. Reg. 1.404(b)-1T) is a payment window, not a filing deadline, so the key stands; the explanation could say 'within 2 1/2 months (by March 15)'.
findings.fix: Optional: phrase the options as 'within 2 1/2 months after year end' to avoid a weekend date.

findings.issue: Rewritten item re-checked blind: answered 'Capitalized with no write-off' before seeing the key. Section 709(a) denies deduction for amounts to promote the sale of interests, and 709(b) amortization covers organizational expenses only. Distractors (180-month amortization, $5,000 deduction) are the organizational-expense rule, which is the right trap. Explanation is accurate.

landing_findings.issue: Checked against the IRS EA FAQ (fetched 2026-11-18): 100 questions, 85 scored and 15 experimental; 3.5 hours; scaled 200 to 800, 500 to pass; window July 1, 2026 to Feb 28, 2027, no testing in March and April; four attempts per part per window; passed parts carry over three years; remote testing only in the U.S.; international testing delayed; 2025 law through December 31, 2025. Landing FAQ and WIRING examFacts agree on all of these. 'Free to start, no account needed.' is present in the hero subtitle. No finding.
2025 bonus depreciation claims (100% after January 19, 2025; 40% for earlier acquisitions placed in service in 2025; election out by class) match the 2025 Instructions for Form 4562. No finding.
